newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania says its coffee being undermined by Kenya.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania says its coffee being undermined by Kenya.

text.p: A senior Tanzanian coffee official on Friday said reports from Kenya were undermining the quality of Tanzania's coffee.

Tanzania Coffee Board spokesman Damian Salla told Reuters Tanzania was concerned about media reports last week in Nairobi quoting Tanzanian farmers as asking the Coffee Board of Kenya to help in farm management techniques to improve quality.
The Coffee Board of Kenya rejected any suggestions that it might be behind moves to undermine Tanzania's coffee quality.
"We would like to strongly reject any claims that we may want to undermine Tanzania," an official told Reuters in Nairobi. "It is not in our interest to do so."
The official added "Our coffee speaks for itself. Our quality is high and we cannot stop anyone from speaking on it."
Salla sharply criticised the Kenyan media for "going on about falling quality of Tanzanian beans without as much as checking with us to ascertain what the simple facts are".

"The Coffee Board of Kenya knows much about Kenyan coffee and its development. We must be expected to know much more about our own coffee than, say, the Kenyans. But no one has spoken to us. That is what is disturbing," Salla said.
"We cannot understand how Tanzanian farmers can possibly tell Kenyan media that they would like to salvage Tanzanian quality via the Kenyan coffee board," Salla said.
On Wednesday, Sannda said that while Tanzanian production was down, quality was clearly up.
"For the quality, it is the best since the liberalisation programme was started (in 1993)," Sannda told Reuters.

Salla said the Tanzania coffee board had nothing to hide as the official Tanzanian body representing the coffee industry and it would welcome any inquiries regarding any quality issues. --Nairobi Newsroom ++254-2 330-261.
